core_obligations: Choose a flat representative (proof lines 12553-12557): by the characterisation of tor amplitude, represent E by a complex E^bullet of flat modules with E^i = 0 outside [a, b].
Pull back (proof lines 12558-12563): then Lf^*E is represented by f^*E^bullet, whose terms are flat by the pullback lemma, so the same characterisation applied to f^*E gives tor amplitude in [a, b].
proof_roadmap: Replace E by a complex of flat modules vanishing outside the interval.
Pull the complex back, use that flatness is preserved, and apply the characterisation again.
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that tor amplitude in a bounded interval is preserved by the derived pullback along a morphism of ringed sites (statement lines 12542-12550). The proof (proof lines 12552-12563) replaces E by a complex of flat modules vanishing outside the interval, pulls it back, and applies the same characterisation to the pulled-back complex. H2: one computation with the characterisation used twice.
